title: Bleeding
wikitext:
{{status
| name = Bleeding
| icon = Bleed status icon.png
| type = Ailment
| description = You are Bleeding, causing you to take Physical Damage over time. The Damage will be higher while you are moving.
}}

'''Bleeding''', or '''bleed''', is an [[ailment]] that deals [[physical damage|physical]] [[damage over time]] to the affected target.<ref name="bleedDebuff"/> [[Moving]] targets suffer increased bleeding damage. Only [[physical damage]] hits can inflict bleed. There are no sources of global chance to bleed or chance to bleed with [[spells]]. Thus, bleed is limited to attack skills only. Bleeding can be Aggravated to cause it to always deal damage as if the target is moving.

==Mechanics==
===Infliction===
Attack will inflict 1 application of '''bleed''' if:
* Base damage of attack have non-zero physical component
* Attack successfully lands (is not blocked, dodged or evaded) {{Citation needed}}
* Attack has a chance to cause bleeding and it passes the chance-check (ex:{{il|Bloodplay}})
** Or attack is guaranteed to cause bleeding (ex:{{il|Farrul's Pounce}})

Different applications of bleed are inflicted independently.

Apart from dealing damage, the '''bleeding''' state (presence of '''bleed''' stacks) can interact with other mechanics ({{il|The Golden Rule}}, {{il|Double Strike}}, {{il|Haemophilia}}).

===Damage===
Bleed deals physical [[damage over time]].

Potential damage from one bleed application is based on the base physical damage of attack that caused it: '''70%''' per second if the target is [[stationary|standing]] still (reduced to 10% if an enemy monster applied it). If the target is [[moving]] or are affected by Aggravated Bleeding, bleeding deals additional damage equal to twice the base, for a total of 3 times the base damage ('''210%''' per second) <ref name="30BleedValues"/>.

By default, only the strongest (the highest damage-per-second) '''bleed''' application will actually deal damage at any given time.

If {{psl|Crimson Dance}} is allocated, the potential damage of one stack is '''35%''' of the inflicting attack's physical damage, regardless of whether the target is moving or not, and the 8 strongest applications will deal damage at any given time. Sustaining all 8 stacks on a target will thus deal an additional '''280%''' of the attack's average physical damage per second. This effectively quadruples bleed DPS in prolonged fights.

Bleed damage is not reduced by [[armour]], but will be reduced by any other sources of physical mitigation, such as [[endurance charge]]s or {{il|Immortal Call}}.

Bleed damage can be increased by the {{il|Vulnerability}} [[hex]].

'''Dual Wielding while using Cleave or Dual Strike:''' If both hands cause bleeding, then the bleeding damage from both hands is combined. If only one hand causes bleeding, then only that hand's bleeding damage will occur.<ref name="BleedWithCleaveOrDualStrike"/>

[[Double damage]] from passives or items like {{il|Paradoxica}} '''does not''' affect bleed damage. Double damage mechanic only modifies the hit damage, not the base damage - so it does not double ailment damage.

===Criticals===

Critical strikes that deal physical damage will not automatically cause bleeding. All physical damage hits must successfully roll chance to bleed to cause bleeding.

Damaging ailments from critical strikes gain a bonus +50% damage over time multiplier, which stacks additively with other sources of damage over time multiplier.<ref>https://www.pathofexile.com/forum/view-thread/2627116</ref> Critical strikes do not directly affect ailment damage otherwise, though it's possible for mechanics to change this: 
* Some stats can add to the DoT multiplier bonus for ailments from critical strikes, such as {{psl|Dire Torment}} or {{il|Critical Strike Affliction Support}}. 
* {{il|Cruelty Support}} grants a damage over time bonus based on hit damage taken by the enemy, which extra damage dealt by critical strikes can contribute to. 
* {{psl|Elemental Overload}} causes ailments to never count as being from critical strikes, removing their bonus. 
* {{psl|Perfect Agony}} causes ailments to use a hit's critical strike multiplier instead of damage over time multiplier. 
** The combination of Elemental Overload and Perfect Agony prevents the application of damaging ailments by hits entirely. 

===Duration===
The base duration of bleed is 5 seconds.<ref name="bleed-on-hit"/> This means that by default and before reductions (see above), an attack that causes bleed will deal an '''additional 350%''' (70% for 5 seconds) over its full duration to a target that isn't moving. If the target is moving for the full duration, this increases to '''1050%''' (350% * 3). If {{psl|Crimson Dance}} is allocated, this additional damage decreases to '''175%''' (350% * 0.5) per stack, regardless of whether the target is moving or not.

Separate applications of bleed do not stack cumulatively (unless {{psl|Crimson Dance}} is allocated, then it stacks up to 8 times). Each bleed effect remains present on the target until it runs its course, but only the one with the highest damage per second will cause damage at any given moment.<ref name="Puncture"/> For example, assume an enemy is inflicted with bleed for 100 damage per second, then after 2 seconds it is inflicted with bleed for 50 damage per second. The outcome will be 500 damage over 5 seconds followed by 100 damage over 2 seconds.

{{il|Temporal Chains}} can be used to slow down expiry of the bleed, as long as they remain cursed. This doesn't reduce DPS, but extends total time bleed deals damage. The default 25% slower expiry—if in effect from the start of the bleed—extends total bleed time and total damage by 33%. At the maximum 75% slower expiry, this goes up to 300% bonus duration / damage. This acts as More modifier, stacking multiplicatively with duration Increases. 

Due to the limited stacking potential of bleed, increasing duration is most effective when it would be difficult for the attacker to simply inflict new bleeds with similar DPS. 

===Aggravate===

Certain effects cause bleeding to be aggravated. Bleeding that is aggravated deals higher damage, as though the target is moving. Aggravate lasts for the remaining duration of the bleed instance.

When bleeding is aggravated, all instances of bleeding on the target become aggravated. The {{c|mod|Chance to Aggravate Bleeding}} is rolled only once for all instances of bleeding and is applied before the bleeding; therefore, if a hit applies bleeding and aggravates at the same time, that instance of bleeding is not aggravated.

The extra damage from aggravated bleeding is separate from the bleeding's normal damage. A 100 DPS bleed that becomes aggravated deals 100 DPS from the bleed effect and 200 DPS from aggravated bleeding. The aggravated damage from that bleed continues to deal damage as long as it's the '''highest aggravated bleed damage''' and the monster '''is stationary'''. <ref>https://www.pathofexile.com/forum/view-thread/3532389</ref>

For example, if you then apply a 200 DPS non-aggravated bleed, the bleed deals:
* 400 DPS while the monster is stationary — {{math|formula=(200 \, \text{bleed} + 200 \, \text{aggravated bleed})
}} 
* 600 DPS while the monster is moving — {{math|formula=(200 \, \text{bleed} \times 3)}}

Aggravated Bleeding grants the same “extra bleeding damage” bonus as the one applied when an enemy is moving. Because these effects are identical, the bonuses '''do not stack'''. <ref>https://www.pathofexile.com/forum/view-thread/3537253</ref>

===Modifiers===
====Damage modifiers====
As a [[damage over time]] effect, bleed's damage can be affected positively or negatively by some damage [[modifier]]s.

The following modifiers will directly affect the damage of bleed:
* {{c|mod|Damage}}
* {{c|mod|Physical Damage}} (including physical damage over time multiplier)
* {{c|mod|Damage over Time}}
* {{c|mod|Bleeding Damage}}
{{c|mod|Trap}}, {{c|mod|mine}}, {{c|mod|minion}} or {{c|mod|totem}} damage modifiers will also affect the damage of bleed if it is applied by a trap, a mine, a minion or a totem respectively.

Also, bleed is non-elemental ailment, so {{c|mod|Damage from Ailments}} modifier will also affect the damage of bleed.

{{c|mod|Flat Physical Attack Damage}} modifiers, being count in base attack damage, also affects bleed damage.

Other modifiers of increased/reduced/more/less type affecting hits ([[attack]], [[melee]], [[ranged]], [[projectile]], etc), as well as any damage modifier specific to the skill, do not apply to bleed.

====Defensive modifiers====
Damage from bleed cannot be affected by mechanics affecting physical damage from hits, such as [[Armour]] or [[Fortify]].

To affect incoming damage from bleed, one need to use global (hits and ailments) or ailment damage reduction modifiers.

Also incoming damage from bleed can be affected by affecting attacker's base physical attack damage, with for example {{il|Lori's Lantern}}.

====Duration modifiers====
Bleed's duration can be affected by following modifiers:
* {{c|mod|Ailment duration}}
* {{c|mod|Bleeding duration}}
* Bleed from {{il|Puncture}} is also affected by {{c|mod|Debuff duration}}

===Removal and immunity===
* a [[flask]] with the {{Ml|FlaskRemovesBleeding1}} [[suffix]] removes bleeding when used and grants immunity to it while active
* {{il|Death's Door}} and {{il|Craiceann's Carapace}} grant immunity to bleeding
* [[Armour and Evasion Mastery]] can grant immune to bleeding if equipped helmet has higher armour than evasion rating
* the skill {{il|Steelskin}} removes bleeding when used and grants immunity to it while active
* {{psl|Adamant}} passive removes bleeding when using a guard skill
* [[Slayer]]'s passive {{psl|Endless Hunger}} grants unaffected by bleeding while [[leech]]ing
*The {{il|Watcher's Eye}} can roll a modifier that grants unaffected by bleeding while affected by {{il|Malevolence}}
*{{il|Kahuturoa's Certainty}} grants unaffected by damaging ailments
*Rings and Belts with an itemlevel of 60 and above can gain the implicit {{c|mod|Bleeding cannot be inflicted on you}} when [[corrupted]].

===Other===
* The {{il|Bloodlust}} support increases melee damage against bleeding enemies, but prevents the skill itself from causing bleeding.
* The {{il|Bloodgrip}} unique amulet and the {{il|The Infinite Pursuit}} unique boots prevent the extra bleed damage taken by movement.

==Version history==
{{Version history table header}}
{{Version history table row|3.25.0|
* Added a new keyword, Aggravate, which causes Bleeding which has been Aggravated to deal more damage as if the target is moving.
}}
{{Version history table row|3.19.0|
* Minions no longer have hidden penalties to Bleeding, Ignite, and Poison damage. Summon Reaper no longer has a hidden bonus to Bleeding damage that counteracted this penalty. As a result, minions now deal approximately twice as much Poison damage, three and a half times as much Ignite damage, and seven times as much Bleeding damage.
}}
{{Version history table row|3.9.0|
* Chance to Bleed and Bleed Duration modifiers can no longer roll as suffixes on weapons. The suffix mods that grant increased Bleeding damage now have higher values and also grants some chance to inflict Bleed.
}}
{{Version history table row|3.0.0|
* Bleeding but now deals half damage while the target was stationary, from one sixth its damage. ''(outdated!)'' The ratio remains unchanged for Bleeding caused by monsters.
* Skills calculate their Ignite, Poison or Bleed values as a separate damage value, taken straight from the base and added damage of the skill. This gives skills that deal fire damage a minimum and maximum Ignite Damage per Second value that is rolled on Ignites that the skill causes. Poison, Bleed and Ignite damage values are based on the base damage of the skill, and then affected by appropriate damage modifiers. Some damage modifiers affect both the hit and the Ignite, Poison or Bleed, while some only affect one.
* Bleeding and Poison are now both considered 'Ailments'. This means their durations are only affected by increased bleeding/poison duration modifiers, and the new ailment duration modifier (they are not elemental ailments, so are not affected by the existing modifier to elemental ailments).

}}
{{Version history table end}}
